title: First hearing the blues from Uncle Charlie
summary: Uncle Charlie played blues on the hall piano for the older neighbors; Turner also rode a junk wagon and learned to drive horses.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What was the first blues...the first time you remember hearing the blues?

Well, my Uncle Charlie used to play the blues all the time on the piano so when he come by...we had the piano in the hall there...he would come by and play the piano for us. Everybody would be sittin' around drinkin' home brew, and livin' it up, so it was...the piano was out in the hall, so they had a bunch of apartments there. So the people used to come out in the hall with they home brew and listen to the music. Was a bunch of elderly people there...had about all the fun they could have. So my Uncle Charlie--he come by there and play for the elderly folks. He used to do it about every other day or so. He always come by to see us, to see my momma and my sister and the kids in the neighborhood.

So I used to...had a man had a coupla horses and a wagon...he used to haul stuff around in it, and sometime I'd get on the wagon and ride with him and go 'round and pick up junk...stuff like that. And if anybody wanted to move, we'd move them in his wagon. So I learnt...every once in awhile, I used to let him...he used to let me drive a little bit, you know. I thought that was big kicks.
